scores.evidence: OIDC from CI to the cloud (no long-lived keys) and a secrets manager such as Vault or the cloud provider's.
scores.rationale: Technical claims (OIDC, GitOps promotion, cosign, Argo Rollouts, policy-as-code, SLSA) are accurate; minor imprecision such as 'SLSA level 2–3' and 'CI updates tag' without digest pinning.

scores.evidence: Group services into archetypes. Most teams end up with 3–6, for example Java/Gradle, Node, Go, Python, frontend
scores.rationale: Covers core needs with sensible phasing and pilot, but leaves key choices open (CI engine, repo strategy) and omits explicit exclusions and runner hosted-vs-self decision.

scores.evidence: Automate promotion: CI updates the image tag in the GitOps repo for dev, then promotion to staging and prod happens through a PR or policy.
scores.rationale: Consistent design around golden path templates, GitOps, and policy; some loose ends like undecided CI engine and the wave pilot timeline overlap.

scores.evidence: Done when: the pilot services deploy to prod through the platform with automatic rollback, and the team has run a rollback drill successfully.
scores.rationale: Has done-when criteria, rollback drill, pilot, warn-only gates, but no measurable targets for build time, no validation of runner/cost risks, little post-launch validation.

scores.evidence: the services run in containers on Kubernetes (or something similar), you have a platform team of 4–6 engineers
scores.rationale: States key assumptions (K8s, team size, mix of languages) but not sensitivity to them, and timelines like '5 successful prod deploys' and '10–20 lines' are unqualified.

scores.evidence: Unversioned shared templates. One bad change can break all 50 services at once.
scores.rationale: Covers template blast radius, false-positive gates, rollback on SLO breach, but misses untrusted-PR secrets, CI outage, flaky tests, DB migrations, and artifact tampering details.

scores.evidence: Treat the platform as a product: give it SLOs, an on-call rotation, a changelog, a roadmap and a feedback channel.
scores.rationale: Rollback, platform on-call and dashboards mentioned, but late (Phase 6), with no migration handling, access admin or platform outage plan.

scores.evidence: Add dashboards for DORA metrics, pipeline duration, flaky tests and runner cost.
scores.rationale: Cost is only mentioned as a dashboard; no estimate, hosted vs self-hosted trade-off, or build volume reasoning.

scores.evidence: Make the key decisions: ... make the decisions that are expensive to change later.
scores.rationale: Recognizes expensive decisions and versions templates, but defers them as lists of options without analysis of lock-in or exit paths.

scores.evidence: don't build the whole platform before anyone uses it.
scores.rationale: Uses existing tools, thin end-to-end first; Backstage and SLSA 3 are somewhat optional but deferred to later phases.

scores.evidence: Done when: a "hello world" service can be built, pushed and deployed to dev entirely through the platform.
scores.rationale: Ordered phases with week ranges and checkable done-when outcomes, though tool choices are left open and some phases lack exit criteria.

checklist.evidence: Catalog all 50 services: language, build tool, test coverage, where it deploys... Allow extension points, not forks of the templates.
Run the old and new pipelines side by side for each service until there have been about 5 successful prod deploys on the new one.
CI updates the image tag in the GitOps repo for dev, then promotion to staging and prod happens through a PR or policy.
OIDC from CI to the cloud (no long-lived keys) and a secrets manager such as Vault
image signing (cosign)... policy as code... signed images only, no `:latest` tags... Aim for SLSA supply-chain level 2–3
Add progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts or Flagger) with canary or blue-green releases. Roll back automatically when SLOs or error rates breach thresholds.
Add contract tests (such as Pact) between services, which matters a lot once you have 50 of them
integration tests in short-lived environments... Set up preview environments for each pull request.
Set up CI runners with autoscaling, ephemeral runners and build caching.
Set up CI runners with autoscaling, ephemeral runners and build caching.
Treat the platform as a product: give it SLOs, an on-call rotation... Measure DORA metrics now
Standardize... automated, auditable deployment and promotion.

traps.evidence: Run the old and new pipelines side by side for each service
policy as code... signed images only, no `:latest` tags
OIDC from CI to the cloud (no long-lived keys)
Each service's pipeline config down to roughly 10–20 lines that call the shared template.
CI engine: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Tekton or Jenkins

note: Solid, sensibly phased pilot-first migration plan using existing tools, but thin on cost, untrusted-build security, migrations, flaky tests and concrete targets, with key tool decisions left open.
